title: Predict: Observers During init
hints: Property observers don't fire when a type sets its own property during `init`.
After `init done`, every assignment fires both observers — including via `bump()` and assigning the same value.
jsBridge: Property observers **don't fire** when the property is set in the type's own `init`, but they do fire for later assignments. JS setters fire during the constructor too. It's a common "why didn't my didSet run?" surprise.

compass.q: A JS setter runs even in the constructor. Why did Swift choose not to fire observers in init?
Do observers fire when a *subclass* init sets an inherited property? (Yes, after `super.init`.)
`didSet` vs setting a value in `init` and calling a `configure()` method: which is clearer?
A view model with `didSet { save() }`: does it save the initial value? Should it?
